runs.name: filter
runs.command: thinkthen filter 'Is this a complaint?' --lines < reviews.txt
runs.input:
Arrived a day early. Thank you!
The zipper broke the first time I used it.
Does this come in blue?
The strap snapped on day two.
runs.output:
The zipper broke the first time I used it.
The strap snapped on day two.
runs.see: filter keeps the two complaints: the broken zipper and the snapped strap.

runs.name: filter-means
runs.command: thinkthen filter 'Is this about the item itself?' --lines --true 'Its build, size, color, or parts.' --false 'Delivery, price, or service.' < reviews.txt
runs.input:
Arrived a day early. Thank you!
The zipper broke the first time I used it.
Does this come in blue?
The strap snapped on day two.
runs.output:
The zipper broke the first time I used it.
Does this come in blue?
The strap snapped on day two.
runs.see: The zipper, the color, and the strap are about the item, so they stay. The early delivery drops out.

runs.name: filter-csv
runs.command: thinkthen filter 'Is this a complaint?' --csv --field /comment < reviews.csv
runs.input:
id,comment
R-1,Arrived a day early. Thank you!
R-2,The zipper broke the first time I used it.
R-3,Does this come in blue?
runs.output: {"id":"R-2","comment":"The zipper broke the first time I used it."}
runs.see: Only R-2 complains, and it comes back as one JSON object, id and all.
